The estate’s recovery depends on how the jurisdiction treats a religious refusal of care. Where a sincere religious objection makes declining a transfusion reasonable, the estate can collect full damages for the death that followed the wound the driver caused. Where mitigation is judged by a purely objective standard, the estate can collect only the damages that would have remained after the transfusion, since the physician confirmed she would have fully recovered with treatment.
CONFIDENCE: 72
